title: Michigan's 3rd Congressional District election, 2026
description: Michigan's 3rd Congressional District encompasses parts of Kent, Ottawa, and Muskegon counties, including the cities of Grand Rapids and Muskegon. Incumbent Democratic Rep. Hillary Scholten, first elected in 2022 when she flipped the seat, is seeking a third term. The district has trended Democratic in recent cycles, with Kamala Harris carrying it by eight points in 2024, though it was a Republican stronghold for decades prior. The Republican primary features Terri DeBoer, a longtime West Michigan television meteorologist, and Ryan Cushman, a businessman and Michigan National Guard veteran, with the primary scheduled for August 4, 2026.
polling_note: No public opinion polls found for this specific race as of June 2026. The Cook Political Report rates this race as 'Likely D' as of January 2026.

candidates.name: Hillary Scholten
candidates.summary: Hillary Scholten is the incumbent U.S. Representative for Michigan's 3rd Congressional District, first elected in 2022. She is a former attorney who served in the U.S. Department of Justice under the Obama administration and later worked at the Michigan Immigrant Rights Center. Scholten emphasizes bipartisan solutions, healthcare access, and economic issues affecting working families.

candidates.name: Terri DeBoer
candidates.summary: Terri DeBoer is a longtime West Michigan television meteorologist who has worked at WOOD-TV, FOX-17, WWMT, and WXMI-TV for over three decades. She announced her Republican candidacy in March 2026, emphasizing fiscal responsibility, healthcare price transparency, border security, and parental rights in education. She positions herself as a political outsider and has never held elected office.

candidates.name: Ryan Cushman
candidates.summary: Ryan Cushman is a local businessman and Michigan National Guard veteran who has lived in Michigan's 3rd District most of his life. He is running for Congress as a Republican, focusing on healthcare affordability, inflation and cost-of-living issues, national security, campaign finance reform, and energy policy. He is a married father of five and resides in Tallmadge Township.
